analysis:
The units are base-side excerpts of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json (lines 2005-3777), a public synthetic test-vector fixture. The patch excerpt shows the head change: the json_object vector gains template_input.additional_context {enable_thinking:false}, prompt_token_count drops from 803 to 767, the chain_hashes and token_ids are regenerated, and the 768-token block boundary is removed. Similar small changes appear at other changed ranges (about lines 3805, 3904, 4752, 43739, 44524, 52354, 53139 and 54086 on the head side). The patch is truncated, so I could not see all of them.

Security-wise this is test data only. It holds no secrets, keys, tokens or consumer data, and the content is explicitly public synthetic text. It changes no authorization, attestation, encryption or App Attest logic (TB-011, TB-002, A-016 are unaffected), and it opens no new endpoint or parsing path in the fixture itself.

The remaining question is the consumer code. It is not supplied. It determines whether prompt-contract ID, template inputs and prefix-cache chain hashes (T-041 cross-tenant cache and timing) are computed consistently. The fixture hashes are computed with the same prompt_contract_id, 8171fec3..., as before, even though the template output changed. Whether that ID should be bumped is a question for the template and contract code. I cannot verify it, and a stale ID would at most be a correctness or cache-keying issue, not an observable vulnerability here. I found no concrete security regression in the supplied evidence.
